sources.entry: Inferable - Open-source managed agent runtime for distributed AI agents

summary.one_liner: Inferable is an open-source managed durable execution runtime for building AI workflows that include human approval steps, with the control plane and SDKs in one repository.
summary.what_it_does: Inferable lets you define versioned, long-running AI workflows in TypeScript or Go, with the Node.js SDK as the main documented option. Workflows run in your own infrastructure and connect via long polling, so no inbound ports need to be opened and no separate deployment step is required. You can create structured LLM outputs that are automatically parsed, validated, and retried on failure. Workflows can pause for human approval, with requests sent via Slack or Email, and resume with preserved context. The repository includes the control plane service, a playground and management console app, a CLI (alpha), and SDKs for Node.js, Go, and .NET (experimental). The README also mentions notifications, memoized results for side-effects, timeline observability, and agent creation.
use_cases: Build AI workflows that wait for human approval before acting
Get structured JSON output from an LLM with validation and retries
Run AI workflows inside a private network or VPC without opening inbound ports
Roll out changes to long-running workflows gradually using versions
Send approval requests or notifications to people via Slack or Email
Cache results of expensive or side-effecting steps in a distributed workflow
how_to_run: Follow the quick start guide linked in the README
Install the Node.js SDK from NPM or the Go SDK (see quick start)
Self-host the control plane using the self hosting guide
notable: Workflows run in your own infrastructure using long polling, with no inbound ports needed
Versioned workflows keep version affinity for executions already in progress
Human-in-the-loop interrupts for approval via Slack or Email with preserved context
Structured LLM outputs with automatic parsing, validation, and retries
Fully open source and self-hostable under MIT
caveats: CLI is marked alpha and the .NET SDK is marked experimental
Go and Node.js are the only language SDKs listed as supported; more languages are said to be coming soon
Self-hosting requires setting up your own infrastructure; the README points to a separate guide for details
keywords: run ai in my own infrastructure
get approval before ai deletes data
